answer: Behavioral island clustering audit. Agents record a sparse contact set; after the fact, identities whose interaction graphs form tight island communities sharing few cross-links get flagged as one operator. A clone cluster leaves a ripple in co-activity residuals relative to the broader graph. Each flagged identity forces the attacker to supply independent, non-overlapping histories that defeat the clustering, and any shared fable of provenance collapses the group at once.
